the OECD countries have a responsibility to ensure that their imported oil is produced and transported in safe conditions.
the OECD countries are not only consuming more than they produce, but also that the majority of their fatalities are imported.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the fatality rates of OECD countries are higher than those of non-OECD ones, which is contrary to what is generally believed and reported.
, in the case of oil consumption, OECD countries are not as safe as their production-based fatality rates suggest.

the consumption-based accounting method is a useful tool to assess the impacts of energy production and trade.
the OECD countries have been able to reduce their own fatality rates by outsourcing the majority of the risk to the non-OECD.
